DOCUMENTS.title: RFC-001: Auth v3 token design
DOCUMENTS.summary: Short-lived access tokens (15m) plus rotating refresh tokens, replacing long-lived session cookies. Defines the dual-validate window and the partner IdP escape hatch.
DOCUMENTS.author: person:priya

DOCUMENTS.title: RFC-002: Event sourcing for the ledger
DOCUMENTS.summary: Proposes event sourcing as the source of truth for the ledger with read-only projections. Motivated by audit requirements and the cost of double-entry write contention.
DOCUMENTS.author: person:tomasz

DOCUMENTS.title: RFC-003: Canonical event envelope
DOCUMENTS.summary: One envelope shape for every event: id, tenant, occurred_at, actor, payload_version. Every producer must emit it for downstream consumers.
DOCUMENTS.author: person:fatima

DOCUMENTS.title: Design: API gateway routing and shedding
DOCUMENTS.summary: How the gateway routes, applies per-tenant limits, and sheds load when downstream auth latency crosses the error budget.
DOCUMENTS.author: person:marcus

DOCUMENTS.title: Design: checkout 3DS challenge flow
DOCUMENTS.summary: Client state machine for 3DS challenges, including the Safari redirect edge case and the webhook-driven recovery path.
DOCUMENTS.author: person:nina

DOCUMENTS.title: Postmortem: auth latency spike on Oct 3
DOCUMENTS.summary: A bad connection-pool change tripled token validation latency for 41 minutes. Contributing factors: no SLO burn alert, and the gateway did not shed load.
DOCUMENTS.author: person:marcus

DOCUMENTS.title: Postmortem: notification retry storm
DOCUMENTS.summary: An SMS provider outage triggered unbounded retries, exhausting the notification connection pool and delaying receipts.
DOCUMENTS.author: person:aisha

DOCUMENTS.title: Runbook: auth token revocation
DOCUMENTS.summary: Steps to revoke all tokens for a tenant, expected blast radius, and how to verify that the gateway has picked up the revocation.
DOCUMENTS.author: person:priya

DOCUMENTS.title: ADR-009: Primary datastore is PostgreSQL
DOCUMENTS.summary: We evaluated Postgres, MySQL, Cassandra and CockroachDB. Chose Postgres for transactional guarantees and operational simplicity; shards handled by logical partitioning per tenant.
DOCUMENTS.author: person:dan

DOCUMENTS.title: ADR-010: Kafka as the event backbone
DOCUMENTS.summary: Kafka over RabbitMQ for the event backbone: replay for audit, and enough throughput for the pipeline. Cost is operational complexity.
DOCUMENTS.author: person:fatima

DOCUMENTS.title: RFC-011: Ledger retention and archival
DOCUMENTS.summary: Hot/cold split: 13 months hot in Postgres, older partitions archived to object storage and queryable on demand.
DOCUMENTS.author: person:tomasz

DOCUMENTS.title: Design: notification fan-out
DOCUMENTS.summary: Channel abstraction, per-tenant quotas, exponential backoff with jitter, and a dead-letter queue with replay tooling.
DOCUMENTS.author: person:aisha

DOCUMENTS.title: Design: online ranking and feature serving
DOCUMENTS.summary: Two-stage ranking: cheap retrieval then a re-ranker. Feature freshness budgets and the fallback when the feature store is unavailable.
DOCUMENTS.author: person:gabriel

DOCUMENTS.title: RFC-014: Partner identity federation
DOCUMENTS.summary: How partner IdPs map onto Meridian accounts, including entitlement sync and the conflict rule when both sides change within the same hour.
DOCUMENTS.author: person:yuki

DOCUMENTS.title: Runbook: Sev-1 payments incident
DOCUMENTS.summary: First-response checklist for payment-path incidents: freeze deploys, check ledger integrity, then decide whether to degrade or fail closed.
DOCUMENTS.author: person:elena

DOCUMENTS.title: Design: catalog index refresh
DOCUMENTS.summary: Incremental indexing from the event stream, plus the nightly full rebuild that repairs drift.
DOCUMENTS.author: person:oskar

DOCUMENTS.title: ADR-017: Gateway and auth stay in Go
DOCUMENTS.summary: Keep the request path in Go for tail latency; services stay in their existing languages. Revisit if the polyglot cost becomes the bottleneck.
DOCUMENTS.author: person:dan

DOCUMENTS.title: Postmortem: checkout conversion drop
DOCUMENTS.summary: A gateway rate-limit change throttled checkout for large tenants; conversion fell 4% for two hours before rollback.
DOCUMENTS.author: person:liam

DOCUMENTS.title: RFC-019: One trace ID across services
DOCUMENTS.summary: Propagate a W3C traceparent from the gateway into every downstream call, so a single query can reconstruct a payment's full path.
DOCUMENTS.author: person:marcus

DOCUMENTS.title: Design: self-serve analytics
DOCUMENTS.summary: Semantic layer and curated marts so growth can answer funnel questions without a data-team ticket.
DOCUMENTS.author: person:isaac

DECISIONS.title: Adopt Auth v3 short-lived tokens
DECISIONS.rationale: Long-lived sessions were our largest blast radius in the Oct 3 latency incident. 15-minute tokens cap the damage from any token leak, and the dual-validate window lets us migrate partner IdPs without a flag day.

DECISIONS.title: Use PostgreSQL as the primary datastore
DECISIONS.rationale: Postgres gave us multi-row transactions and mature tooling at the lowest operational cost. Cassandra was faster to scale out but lost us atomic multi-account transfers; CockroachDB cost roughly 3x for features we did not need yet.

DECISIONS.title: Adopt Kafka as the event backbone
DECISIONS.rationale: Audit replay was the deciding factor: we need to reconstruct any ledger state from scratch. Kafka's retention model fits that; RabbitMQ did not.

DECISIONS.title: Make the ledger event-sourced
DECISIONS.rationale: Audit asked for the full history of every balance change. Event sourcing with immutable entries gives that for free and turns reconciliation into a replay. The cost is read-model complexity, which we absorb with projections.

DECISIONS.title: Keep the gateway and auth in Go
DECISIONS.rationale: Tail latency on the request path is a product problem, not just an SRE one. Go gave us predictable p99s with far less tuning than the Python services we benchmarked.

DECISIONS.title: Gateway sheds load rather than failing closed
DECISIONS.rationale: During the Oct 3 incident the gateway kept sending requests to a degraded auth service and made the outage worse. Proposed fix: shed on auth latency and serve cached session checks for a short grace window.

DECISIONS.title: Replace global rate limits with per-tenant limits
DECISIONS.rationale: The conversion-drop postmortem showed one large tenant exhausting the shared bucket and starving everyone else. Per-tenant buckets are fairer and make abuse isolation possible.

DECISIONS.title: No first-party mobile app this year
DECISIONS.rationale: Mobile checkout converts at roughly half of web with the current 3DS flow, and fixing that is a prerequisite. We would rather spend the quarter on the web checkout and the auth migration.

DECISIONS.title: Scope idempotency keys to the tenant
DECISIONS.rationale: A single global key space let one tenant's retry reject another's request. Tenant-scoped keys plus a 72-hour window removed the collision class entirely.

DECISIONS.title: Identity sync stays owned by Platform, not Payments
DECISIONS.rationale: Both teams depend on it, so neither owning it worked. Platform owns it and Payments consumes it as an internal API with an SLA.

DECISIONS.title: Notifications use exponential backoff with a DLQ
DECISIONS.rationale: The retry storm postmortem showed unbounded retries against a dead provider. Bounded exponential backoff plus a dead-letter queue with replay tooling keeps one provider outage from becoming a pool exhaustion.

DECISIONS.title: Two-stage ranking instead of a single deep model
DECISIONS.rationale: The deep model added 40ms p99 for a 1.8% lift. Two-stage retrieval plus re-ranking hit most of that gain inside the latency budget, and the cheap stage degrades gracefully when features are missing.

DECISIONS.title: Archive ledger partitions older than 13 months
DECISIONS.rationale: Postgres table bloat was the top source of ledger write latency. Moving cold partitions to object storage cut p99 writes by 40%.

DECISIONS.title: Standardise on W3C traceparent everywhere
DECISIONS.rationale: Debugging a payment meant correlating four log formats. A single trace id across the gateway, payments and the ledger makes it one query.

DECISIONS.title: Build a self-serve analytics layer for Growth
DECISIONS.rationale: Every funnel question became a data-team ticket, and the queue was the bottleneck for the growth experiments. A semantic layer plus curated marts removed the dependency.

MESSAGES.author: person:priya
MESSAGES.content: RFC-001 is up for review. The short part: 15 minute access tokens, rotating refresh tokens, and a 6 week dual-validate window.

MESSAGES.author: person:dan
MESSAGES.content: Read it twice. The dual-validate window is what makes this safe — flag day would have been reckless.

MESSAGES.author: person:yuki
MESSAGES.content: Partner IdPs are the hard part. identity-sync needs to accept both token shapes during the window, so MER-1003 is on me.

MESSAGES.author: person:marcus
MESSAGES.content: Once auth changes shape, the gateway has to keep validating the old tokens too. That is MER-1004 and it blocks checkout work.

MESSAGES.author: person:sofia
MESSAGES.content: Half of our alerting still keys off the old session header. We will need to update the gateway dashboards too.

MESSAGES.author: person:tomasz
MESSAGES.content: Ledger write path depends on the auth scope being present on every entry. Adding scope checks under MER-1005 before the token change lands.

MESSAGES.author: person:elena
MESSAGES.content: Quarterly plan is up. Auth v3 is the spine of the quarter and most of Payments is behind it.

MESSAGES.author: person:chloe
MESSAGES.content: internal callers on API keys — MER-1006 has to land the same week as the cutover or they start 401ing in prod.

MESSAGES.author: person:ravi
MESSAGES.content: Agreed. I would rather do one coordinated cutover with a bake than two.

MESSAGES.author: person:yuki
MESSAGES.content: Federation RFC draft is out. Conflict rule: if both sides change within an hour, Meridian wins until the partner catches up.

MESSAGES.author: person:priya
MESSAGES.content: That is a reasonable default. Please add the retry backoff for the partner side though.

MESSAGES.author: person:aisha
MESSAGES.content: Unsubscribe tokens need to survive rotation or every auth release re-subscribes everyone. MER-1007.

MESSAGES.author: person:nina
MESSAGES.content: From the checkout side: please do not change the session cookie shape without telling us, the retry path depends on it.

MESSAGES.author: person:oskar
MESSAGES.content: Search caches session-scoped results. After the cutover we will need a reindex, tracked as MER-1008.

MESSAGES.author: person:fatima
MESSAGES.content: Reminder for everyone: every event now needs the RFC-003 envelope. No envelope, no downstream consumer.

MESSAGES.author: person:gabriel
MESSAGES.content: That is MER-1041. The ranking retrain is blocked until the pipeline lands exactly-once.

MESSAGES.author: person:hana
MESSAGES.content: Exactly-once on the ledger stream is the hard part. Chained transactions across Postgres and Kafka.

MESSAGES.author: person:tomasz
MESSAGES.content: Ledger projections are landing this sprint. Balance queries stop touching the write tables.

MESSAGES.author: person:ravi
MESSAGES.content: Payout reconciliation is still manual — MER-1011. Comparing against the partner statement every month by hand.

MESSAGES.author: person:elena
MESSAGES.content: Let us get the replay-based reconciliation from RFC-002 instead of more manual comparison.

MESSAGES.author: person:ravi
MESSAGES.content: Idempotency collisions are fixed. Tenant-scoped keys, MER-1012 closing today.

MESSAGES.author: person:chloe
MESSAGES.content: Confirmed fixed in staging. Two tenants were sharing a key space before, so a retry from one rejected the other.

MESSAGES.author: person:nina
MESSAGES.content: Out-of-order refund webhooks still bite us — MER-1013. The UI shows a refunded charge as pending.

MESSAGES.author: person:liam
MESSAGES.content: Checkout is our highest-converting surface, so that one matters more than its priority suggests.

MESSAGES.author: person:dan
MESSAGES.content: Multi-currency rounding is a correctness bug waiting to happen. MER-1014 should be P1 not P2.

MESSAGES.author: person:tomasz
MESSAGES.content: Fair. The rounding happens at the projection edge, so it interacts with the event sourcing work.

MESSAGES.author: person:marcus
MESSAGES.content: Auth latency spike postmortem is published. 41 minutes, 3x token validation p99, and we had no burn alert.

MESSAGES.author: person:dan
MESSAGES.content: The gateway kept sending traffic to a degraded auth. We need to shed, not queue.

MESSAGES.author: person:marcus
MESSAGES.content: Filed the proposal for fail-open + load shedding. Short version: shed on auth latency, serve cached checks for a grace window.

MESSAGES.author: person:dan
MESSAGES.content: Approved with changes — never serve a cached session check for a write path. Reads only.

MESSAGES.author: person:marcus
MESSAGES.content: SLO burn alerts for the token endpoint are in — MER-1021. We page at 2x burn for 5 minutes.

MESSAGES.author: person:sofia
MESSAGES.content: Per-tenant rate limits are specced. One tenant should not be able to spend everyone else's budget.

MESSAGES.author: person:liam
MESSAGES.content: That was the conversion drop. We rolled back but the fix is the per-tenant limit.

MESSAGES.author: person:priya
MESSAGES.content: Token revocation runbook is written. Revoke for a tenant, then verify the gateway has picked it up.

MESSAGES.author: person:marcus
MESSAGES.content: Added a check for that to the runbook — the gateway caches revocation state for 30s.

MESSAGES.author: person:aisha
MESSAGES.content: Notification retry storm postmortem. Unbounded retries against a dead SMS provider ate the connection pool.

MESSAGES.author: person:ravi
MESSAGES.content: That storm delayed payment receipts too — the notification service is on the payments path.

MESSAGES.author: person:aisha
MESSAGES.content: Right, so backoff with jitter plus a DLQ. Decision is accepted, implementation is MER-1032.

MESSAGES.author: person:nina
MESSAGES.content: 3DS challenge loop on Safari is the top checkout bug. It is MER-1030 and it is a redirect problem, not a payments problem.

MESSAGES.author: person:chloe
MESSAGES.content: Can confirm from the server side: the challenge callback lands, we just never see the result. Webhook timing.

MESSAGES.author: person:dan
MESSAGES.content: Chaos test on auth during peak checkout is blocked until the load shedding work lands. That is the right order.

MESSAGES.author: person:hana
MESSAGES.content: Partition pruning regression on the ledger table — MER-1042. New partition key made the planner re-scan.

MESSAGES.author: person:fatima
MESSAGES.content: Archive job should fix it. Cold partitions off the hot table means the planner has less to reason about.

MESSAGES.author: person:marcus
MESSAGES.content: Trace propagation RFC is up. W3C traceparent from the gateway into every downstream call.

MESSAGES.author: person:ravi
MESSAGES.content: Please include the ledger write path. Reconciling four log formats by hand is how we found the refund ordering bug.

MESSAGES.author: person:gabriel
MESSAGES.content: Two-stage ranking is the call. Deep model was 40ms p99 for a 1.8% lift — not worth it in checkout.

MESSAGES.author: person:zoe
MESSAGES.content: Agreed, and the retrieval stage degrades gracefully when the feature store is cold, which happens at peak.

MESSAGES.author: person:isaac
MESSAGES.content: Self-serve analytics is live. Growth can answer funnel questions without a data ticket now.

MESSAGES.author: person:liam
MESSAGES.content: That unblocks us. Ask and you shall receive, without waiting a sprint.

MESSAGES.author: person:elena
MESSAGES.content: Reminder: Sev-1 payments runbook assumes deploy freeze first, then ledger integrity, then degrade or fail closed. Read it before your next on-call.
